title: Generation & Retrieval Endpoint Requirements, Acceptance Matrix, and Go/No-Go Runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Finalize product-level behavioral requirements and an operational go/no-go runbook for the hosted generation and retrieval endpoints surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). This ticket captures clarified scope, non-negotiable acceptance gates, test coverage expectations, and the progressive rollout strategy for the hosted API launch window.

Scope:
- Chat (streaming & non-streaming): conversation state, function/tool call compatibility, structured output schema enforcement.
- Completions (single-turn): deterministic seeding for tests, temperature/ sampling controls, max tokens accounting.
- Embeddings: canonical dimensionality and normalization options, stable model-version contract.
- Rerank: scoring contract (float range), tie-breaking determinism, per-request top-k selection semantics.

Out of scope for this ticket: client SDK ergonomics, Dedicated autoscaling policy tuning, on-prem packaging changes. Those are tracked separately but may be referenced as dependencies.

Key clarifications from recent PM/DSE syncs:
- The hosted API will return a top-level "model_version" header with every response for debug and billing reconciliation.
- Streaming responses must include interim chunk ids for reassembly; clients MAY ignore but the contract must be documented.
- Embedding vectors will be returned as base64-encoded arrays in the initial launch to reduce client parsing differences across languages (SDKs will unwrap).
- Rerank will accept either raw-score arrays or precomputed embeddings + candidate list; canonicalization will happen server-side and recorded in logs for audits.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Behavioral correctness:
- Chat: full conversation replay test passes for 95% of canonical test prompts (deterministic seed where applicable).
- Completions: length, stop-token behavior, and structured-json output validated against schema for 100% of defined grammar prompts.
- Embeddings: vectors have expected dimensionality (512/1536 as per model) and cosine similarity tolerances within +/-0.02 vs reference harness.
- Rerank: top-k ordering matches reference harness 98% of the time across 10k sampled requests.

2) Performance & SLOs (hosted tier):
- P99 latency for 512-token chat <= 400ms for warm requests; P50 <= 60ms.
- Embedding generation P99 <= 120ms for single item.
- Throughput validated at target concurrency (XPS) with <1% error rate for 60-minute soak.

3) Observability & tracing:
- Per-request model_version, route, and cost_token_count emitted to tracing header and visible in Console.
- Golden metrics dashboards instrumented and verified: latency, error-rate, token cost breakdown, cold-start rate.

4) Safety & rate-limits:
- Abuse detection heuristics enabled for launch tenants; backpressure behavior documented and tested.
- Quota enforcement returns defined 429 payload schema.

5) Security & compliance:
- KMS-backed key usage for any customer-provided keys verified in Private/Dedicated migrations.
- Audit log sample ingestion validated end-to-end into the compliance sink.

6) Ops readiness:
- Runbook steps for degraded model fallback (to smaller quantized variant) tested in staging.
- Runbook lists required on-call rotations and escalation paths.

7) Docs & SDKs:
- Public API reference pages exist and include behavioral examples for edge cases (stop tokens, streaming disconnects, rerank tie-breakers).
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (Internal Canary - week 1):
- Deploy endpoint behind feature flag to 5 internal teams and Redwood test harness.
- Run 12-hour soak with golden prompts, synthetic spikes, and canary dashboards.

Phase 1 (Beta - week 2-3):
- Gradual percentage rollout (1% -> 5% -> 20%) to self-serve accounts with usage caps.
- Monitor: latency, error budget burn, model mismatch regressions.
- Gating: must meet acceptance criteria 1-4 and error budget < 0.1% burned.

Phase 2 (General availability):
- Remove feature flag and enable default routing for newly created hosted endpoints.
- Customers on older contract versions get opt-in migration prompts.

Progression gates: each phase requires an approval from PM + Eng lead + SRE + Security (email approval stored in this ticket).
test_plan:
E2E test harness components:
- Deterministic replay runner: replays recorded customer-ish traces (sanitized) and compares model outputs against approved baselines.
- Fuzzing suite: malformed json, truncated streams, high-concurrency bursts to validate graceful degradation.
- Integration tests: Console create-route -> API call -> billing record verification.
- Load tests: ramp to 2x projected launch QPS and run 1-hour sustained soak.
- Regression tests: embedding similarity regression checks using held-out evaluation set; rerank order stability checks.

Acceptance for tests: test bundles must be runnable in CI and pass on the release branch. Any flaky test must have an associated ENG ticket open before merging to main.
monitoring_and_observability:
- Dashboards: latency by model_version, error-class (client, server, infra), token-cost heatmap, top failing prompts.
- Alerts: SLO breach (error budget), P99 latency > threshold, downstream infra errors > 5% over 5 minutes.
- Tracing: single-trace view from Console should reconstruct streaming sessions and show model kernel selection.
- Audit logs: request metadata (tenant_id, model_version, route, tokens billed) persisted 30 days for hosted by default.
- Postmortem: any production incident during rollout must follow the 72-hour blameless postmortem cadence.
rollback_conditions:
Immediate rollback to previous model variant or disable risky surface if any of the following occur:
- Sustained error-rate > 1% for 15 minutes and not attributable to external dependency.
- P99 latency exceedance for 30 minutes with > 30% increase vs baseline.
- Critical correctness regression: rerank ordering shift > 5% from baseline on safety-critical test suite.
- Security alert flagged by SecOps requiring isolation.

Rollback steps (short):
1) Feature-flag off or route traffic to fallback.
2) Notify on-call, PM, and affected customers.
3) Triage logs and collect traces for triage runbook.
4) Post-rollback verification: run targeted regression suite and confirm metrics back to baseline.
